p.title: Who rules? Monarchy or not?
p.challenge: Sort each country or description by its kind of government, then press Check.

items.why: The UK has a monarch whose powers are limited by law.
Japan is a constitutional monarchy.
Bhutan has a king and an elected parliament that makes laws under a constitution.

items.text: King's powers limited; parliament makes laws
items.why: A monarch limited by a constitution: constitutional monarchy.

items.text: The monarch holds almost all power
items.why: That is an absolute monarchy.

items.text: Head of state is elected, not born to rule
items.why: In a monarchy the position passes down in the family; an elected head is not a monarch.

items.text: A gaṇa: power shared among a group
items.why: Ancient Indian gaṇas shared power among a group, not one monarch.

p.title: Compare governments

items.why: In a democracy people choose and change rulers through elections.

items.text: Free press, courts and rights for citizens
items.why: A democracy protects citizens with courts, a free press and rights.

items.text: One person took power without an election
items.why: One ruler not chosen in free and fair elections: dictatorship.

items.text: Ruler bans newspapers that criticise him
items.why: In a dictatorship people usually cannot criticise the ruler freely.

items.text: A small group of the very rich rules
items.why: Rule by a small group of powerful people: oligarchy.

items.text: A few military leaders rule together
items.why: A small group such as military leaders rules: oligarchy.
Rule by religious leaders: theocracy.

items.text: Laws based on the rules of one religion
items.why: Laws based on one religion: theocracy.
